public_rationale: The [ServiceNow disclosure](https://newsroom.servicenow.com/press-releases/details/2024/ServiceNow-to-unlock-247-productivity-at-massive-scale-with-AI-agents-for-IT-Customer-Service-Procurement-HR-Software-Development-and-more-09-10-2024-traffic/default.aspx) documents customer-created skills, and Atlassian described bespoke agent construction. That supports the narrower observation that customization involves work. It does not show that all ordinary deployments required programming, or that configured systems could not make runtime choices. The stronger claim remains unsettled.
limitations: No-code is not equivalent to no configuration.
Configuration and limited autonomy can coexist.
The rhetorical comparison with lifeforms is not a measurable intelligence test.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Enterprise AI 'agents' are not intelligent decision-makers but automations that customers must spend time programming.

statement.excerpt: These "agents" are branded to sound like intelligent lifeforms that can make intelligent decisions, but are really just trumped-up automations that require enterprise customers to invest time programming them.

from_speaker: branded to sound like intelligent lifeforms
require enterprise customers to invest time programming them
our_interpretation: Intelligent lifeforms is rhetorical language. The checkable core concerns advertised decision-making and the customer work required to make the agents function.
The plain reading of programming includes specifying instructions, actions, and workflows through code or visual and natural-language tools.
Optional customization does not prove that programming is required for ordinary use.
Customer setup does not by itself show that all runtime decisions are predetermined.
For this ongoing observation, I use the September 2024 announcement cycle through publication.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous deployment evidence shows that ordinary use required customers to construct the decision workflows, and that the agents followed those workflows without the advertised ability to select task steps dynamically.
criteria.contradiction_condition: An in-scope agent demonstrably selected and completed task steps without customer-authored decision workflows, or ordinary deployment did not require the programming asserted.

evidence.locator: Developing custom Now Assist skills and underlying prompts to tailor use cases natively within the Now Platform
evidence.explanation: The announcement confirms customer-created skills and prompts as part of the proposed system. It describes customization as an option and places the first agent releases in November, so it does not prove mandatory programming or observed September decision behavior.

evidence.locator: Superpower your workflows with virtual teammates — Versatile and easy to create
evidence.explanation: Atlassian offered a route for customer-authored behavior, while the same section anticipated prebuilt agents. Neither optional authoring nor a no-code interface establishes whether ordinary customers had to program decision workflows.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Contemporaneous setup guides and deployment recordings showing mandatory customer work, default capabilities, and whether task steps were selected dynamically or fully prescribed.
